brief.headline: Push for ₹290/KG (our best price today) and offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 for a discount worth roughly 11% — they lost money last year and carry heavy debt, so cash is what they need most.

priceAsk.summary: Ask to match ₹290/KG on the key Electral laminates (currently ₹295/KG)
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack for the same laminates (gap 1.7% on top SKUs). The market asking band for pharma ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg — our current ₹295 sits at the top of that fair band, so ₹290 is still market-fair and matches our best internal price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (half our current 30 days) in exchange for a price cut of around 10.96%
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹9.49 L of our cash, but they borrow money at about 10.96% so early payment is worth that rate to them — a fair swap for a discount.

brief.financialLeverage: GLS lost ₹23.68 Cr in FY2024-25 and keeps -3.4% of every rupee they sell (peers keep 2.5%). They owe 2.15 times their own cash (₹208.21 Cr debt) and their borrowing rate is around 10.96%, so cash is tight. Their credit rating is IVR BBB- / Stable and they sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.68). We are only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we are not their lifeline — but their weak money-health score (2/10) and loss-making year mean we must lead with supply security and a second source, not a hard price squeeze that could tip them over.

evidence.figure: ₹-23.68 Cr net profit, -3.4% margin vs 2.5% peer median

evidence.point: They carry heavy debt and barely cover interest
evidence.figure: 2.15x debt-to-equity, 0.06x interest coverage, ₹208.21 Cr total debt

evidence.point: Their credit rating and distress signal show fragility
evidence.figure: IVR BBB- / Stable, Altman Z 1.68 (grey zone), health D (21/100)

evidence.point: We pay ₹3.91 L/year more than our cheapest laminate supplier
evidence.figure: Top gap: LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 07 at ₹295/KG vs ₹290/KG (Shrinath Roto Pack), 1.7% gap, ₹3.35 L excess

evidence.point: They take longer to pay their own suppliers than peers
We are a tiny customer to them
evidence.figure: ₹2.31 Cr spend = 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in tiny volume — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (revenue ₹2611.64 Cr, health C 59/100).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both film substrate and conversion — can second-source at scale (revenue ₹16492.00 Cr, health C 46/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source option (revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health D 31/100).

risks: They are loss-making (₹-23.68 Cr FY2024-25) and carry risk flags (severe legal cases, GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, high leverage 2.1x) — pushing too hard on price could break supply; qualify a second source now.
Their money-health score is 2/10 and credit rating IVR BBB- / Stable — don't put your entire laminate volume through them; split the business.
We are only 0.33% of their revenue, so we have little leverage on price alone — payment terms and volume commitments will move them more.
The Altman Z score of 1.68 puts them in the grey distress zone — any negotiation must balance cost with continuity; avoid actions that tip them into real distress.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to match the ₹290/KG we already pay Shrinath Roto Pack for these laminates — and we're ready to pay you in 15 days instead of 30 if you can give us a discount worth that faster cash.
